description: Recover git work that seems to have vanished, audit what's at risk before deleting anything, verify a branch is genuinely merged, and safely retire old worktrees/clones/stashes. Use whenever the user is panicking about lost work ("I think I lost a commit", "my branch disappeared", "did I just lose my changes", "git reset --hard and now it's gone", "force-pushed over my work", "my stash vanished"), wants to recover something via git reflog or git fsck, or asks whether a branch is safe to delete or "is this actually merged" — especially after a squash merge, where commit counts and `git diff branch...main` both give misleading answers. Also use before any destructive git command (`git branch -D`, `git worktree remove`, `git stash drop`, `rm -rf` on a repo dir), and even when only one checkout is mentioned, since a sibling clone or worktree elsewhere on disk is invisible to a single-checkout `git branch -a` / `git stash list` / `git fsck`.
